cohort: 962 infertile couples undergoing intrauterine insemination treatment at a single center
finding: Male hepatitis B virus infection was not associated with significant differences in standard sperm parameters or pregnancy outcomes but was associated with lower sperm acrosin activity, a higher cesarean delivery rate, and an altered newborn sex ratio.
mod_finding: Male HBV infection was associated with a higher cesarean rate compared to the control group.
